parts:
Hi Jitong,

See my response below. 

On Jan 26, 2018, at 12:13 PM, Lou, Jitong <jit...@live.unc.edu> wrote:

Dear Dr.Jiang,
        I'm using CODEX to analyze copy number changes in mouse samples(mm10), but I have some problems regarding your getmapp.R and mapp.R programs.
1. In getmapp.R, besides "mappability", I notice "mapp_ref" is also a pre-computed list containing IRanges objects for each chromosome of humans, but I couldn't find the program to compute it on Github. Could you send me any illustrative example if you have one?

The current version of CODEX doesn’t have pre-computed mappability for the mouse genome (neither mm9 nor mm10). The end result of getmapp() is just a vector or mappability, with length equal to the number of exons. You can download this from UCSC for example if you don’t want to compute yourself or you can modify mapp.R (see below).

Note that mappability is only used during the QC procedure and doesn’t seem to have too much effect on normalization/segmentation. Another way is to remove exons that are in segmental duplication regions, which correspond to regions with low mappability. Or simply set mappability to 1 for all exons and see if you can recover CNVs that you know are true (TP).

2. In getmapp.R(and getgc.R), I notice you didn't do the computation for chrM. Is it ok if I modify the program to include chrM?  

Not sure if it makes sense to call copy number for chrM (this is our end goal) but yes if needed you can add it. We most likely won't push update on this though.

3. In mapp.R, I notice the results of "mapp" are different from the "mapp_codex"(the corresponding elements in "mappability"). So, in my understanding, "mapp" is a better estimation of mappability, but using "mappability" is good enough and more time-saving. Is it correct?

Hmm, it’s been a while since I touched this code. How different are they? Mapp_codex is by default how we calculate mappability for human hg19. Mapp is what actually should be done but is very time consuming.

4. When I tried to run mapp.R, I got an error which said R couldn't find function elementLengths(). Should I use elementNROWS() or other functions as elementLengths() might be deprecated?

Yes seems like elementLengths() is defunct. 


        Thank you in advance!
Best,
Jitong
